_meta.note: What each dose line's stock does to the nutrient solution, so the dose review can estimate EC and pH after a dose (contract 11.3). ecChangePerMlPerL: the EC rise in mS/cm from 1 mL of stock in 1 L of solution; phChangePerMlPerL: the pH change from the same. Stocks (farm details form, R-1, section 5): N City Greens Grow (24%), P City Greens Grow Flora (26%), K City Greens Grow Thrive (19%), each in a 10 L tank (confirmed at the farm, review of #82). The form's phosphoric acid (pH down, 1 L) has no dose pump: IN4 on both controllers is the water inlet, so it is not a dose line. Each line also says what it is (T1-38): name (what the app shows), compound (the product or salt), strengthPct (its strength as sold or mixed, % w/v), drum (the container the stock is kept in: id and volumeL), and purpose (what it is dosed for). The pump rate is hardware.json pumps.doseLines.<line>.flowMlPerS, not a copy here. name, compound and strengthPct are the form's (section 5); drum.volumeL is the 10 L tank, confirmed at the farm by Noohu; purpose is proposed for the team to check.

sources.doseLines.N.ecChangePerMlPerL: PLACEHOLDER: client_A's contract-example stock (0.47), until a jar test: 1 mL of the N stock in 1 L of the farm's water, read the EC rise. On the high side on purpose: the review then stops short of the EC ceiling rather than past it.
sources.doseLines.P.ecChangePerMlPerL: PLACEHOLDER: as doseLines.N.ecChangePerMlPerL, for the P stock.
sources.doseLines.K.ecChangePerMlPerL: PLACEHOLDER: as doseLines.N.ecChangePerMlPerL, for the K stock.
sources.doseLines.N.phChangePerMlPerL: PLACEHOLDER: treated as pH-neutral until the jar test also reads the pH.
sources.doseLines.*.purpose: PROPOSED: what each nutrient is usually dosed for; not on the farm details form.
